China’s Weaponization of Dual-Use Research Vessels for Undersea Data Dominance
news.summary_en: Analysis of 223 vessels finds that Chinese research ships spend an unusually large share of time near subsea infrastructure on the high seas. The findings call for stronger allied monitoring, coordinated patrols, and faster cable repair.

news.title: Moving the Texas  Semiconductor Ecosystem to the Next Level
news.summary_en: Texas is reaping the benefits of a wave of AI- and national security–driven capital investments. Scaling Texas’s semiconductor ecosystem will depend on converting these investments into advancements in areas critical to success, including infrastructure.

news.title: Learning Without Bleeding: China’s Lessons from the Russia-Ukraine Drone War
news.summary_en: China is using the Russia-Ukraine drone war as a military laboratory. Lilly Min-Chen Lee and Kateryna Bondar trace how quickly Chinese analysts identify battlefield innovations and how the PLA translates the lessons into training, procurement, hardware, and force structure.

news.title: The Postwar Threat to Gulf Energy Infrastructure
news.summary_en: As Gulf states build new pipelines to reduce Iran’s leverage over the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran is likely to adapt. Pipelines offer greater resilience, but remain vulnerable to Iranian missiles, drones, sabotage, and other attacks on critical energy infrastructure.

news.title: The AI Export Dilemma
news.summary_en: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch discusses whether the United States should allow exports of AI technologies and strategies the United States could employ to stay ahead in the global technology race.

news.summary_en: The U.S. government should empower the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) to be a more effective agency to lead on economic growth abroad.

news.title: The Self-Reliance Dividend: The Imperative of Syrian Refugees’ Economic Inclusion
news.summary_en: The current model for refugee management has failed. Will Todman argues that Gulf and Western actors should advance a new approach that prioritizes Syrian refugees’ self-reliance and private sector integration, making them part of the regional connectivity agenda.

news.title: Space Intelligence: The Foundation of Space Superiority
news.summary_en: Space superiority depends on knowing what adversaries can do and recognizing when their behavior changes. Persistent collection and analysis across government, industry, and allies can help anticipate threats before they materialize.
